SECTION ONE
Purpose and Scope
Purpose
Article 1-(1) The purpose of this Directive is to regulate the principles regarding the purpose, area of activity, ways of
work, duties, authorities and responsibilities, operations, and objectives of Gebze Technical University (GTU)
Sustainability Coordination Office.
Scope
Article 2 -(1) This Directive covers the provisions regarding the establishment and implementation of university
policies on green space s, natural environment, waste, energy, water, transportation, accessibility, education, smart
campus and digital applications, and sustainable behaviors within the scope of "sustainable campus" at GTU.
Basis
Article 3-(1) This Directive has been prepared based on the Environment Law No. 2872, Article 12 of the Zero Waste
Regulation published in the Official Gazette dated 12/07/ 2019 and numbered 30829, Article 14 of the Higher
Education Law No. 2547, the Paris Climate Agreement, and the European Green Deal.
Definitions
Article 4-(1) In this Directive, the following terms have the following definitions:
a) Division: All academic and administrative divisions within GTU
b) Supreme Commission: GTU Sustainable Campus Supreme Commission
c) Commission: GTU Sustainable Campus Commission
d) Coordinator: GTU Sustainability Office Coordinator
e) Coordination Office: GTU Sustainability Coordination Office
f) Center: Centers established within GTU
g) Rector: GTU Rector
h) University: GTU
SECTION TWO
Objectives and Areas of Activity of the Coordination Office
Objectives of the Coordination Office
Article 5-(1) The objectives of the Coordination Office are as follows:
a) To conduct research, follow innovations, and manage processes in order to develop sustainable policies in the fields
of ecosystem, life, environment and human health, management and research and development at the university
b) To contribute to the development of awareness of efficient and sustainable resource use among university
employees and students and to disseminate innovative approaches for this purpose
c) To carry out studies to establish a green campus and sustainable corporate governance approach, to ensure that the
university continues its development without compromising on its sustainability goals , to ensure that research and
development projects, industrial collaborations, education and training activities, social activities and initiatives at the
university are organized and carried out in a way that includes sustainability principles
d) To act with the awareness of being a sustainable institution for a sustainable world, to determine the strengths and
weaknesses of the university in terms of sustainability by paying attention to all sustainable development goals set by
the United Nations, and to identify priority areas. To be a driving force for the university to stand out as a strong and
sustainable institution, especially by focusing on issues such as education, equality, health, combating climate change
and its effects, waste treatment and recycling, energy saving
e) To work in cooperation with the commission, divisions, and centers of th e u niversity related to sustainability
principles, to increase the exchange of information among these divisions, and to continue sustainability activities with

f) To work to increase the number of projects related to sustainability policies at the university, to follow national and
international project calls, to work in cooperation with the commissions, divisions, and centers of the university
operating in this field, and to encourage our academics
g) To ensure the participation of undergraduate and graduate students in the processes, to organize student societies in
order to integrate sustainability awareness into campus life, and to realize the related goals
Areas of Activity of the Coordination Office
Article 6-(1) The areas of activity of the Coordination Office are as follows:
a) Managing sustainability activities at the u niversity, ensuring coordination , and increasing cooperation among the
university’s centers, commissions, and divisions related to sustainability , monitorin g the activities of these
commissions and divisions in order to prepare a detailed and informative sustainability report, and ensuring that all
activities are reported on time
b) Preparing and updating the website to share sustainability and green campus activities with the public
c) Organizing seminars and symposiums on sustainability, following innovations, informing staf f and students about
activities
d) Informing the relevant divisions and encouraging academics to integrate the concept of sustainability in education
and training, increasing the number of courses directly related or related to sustainability, a nd organizing learning
outcomes
e) Following the calls for projects on sustainability, determining the conditions for applying to these projects,
establishing teams and making project applications, working in coordination with the relevant divisions on this issue
f) Carrying out studies for the preparation of the Climate Action Plan
g) Within the scope of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, assisting the relevant divisions of the
Rectorate in identifying students struggling with these problems in order to reduce hunger and poverty
h) Drawing attention to gender equality at the university and raising awareness for the protection of the rights of
minorities, increasing activities to raise awareness of staff and students by working with the relevant divisions on this
issue
i) For a sustainable and healthy environment and a sustainable life, determining the needs of students and staff such as
water, electricity, cleaning, transportation, food , and shelter in the first place and guiding the creation of policies to
meet these needs
j) Developing responsible consumption awareness, conducting awareness activities to instill the importance of saving
in the use of resources such as water and electricity, drawing attention to campus cleanliness, and raising awar eness of
students on this issue
k) Instilling recycling awareness, supporting studies on the production and design of recyclable products, encouraging
the use of recyclable products, involving company representatives or academics carrying out projects on this subject in
sustainability studies
l) Drawing attention to the disposal of hazard ous waste for the protection of natural life, taking initiatives to identify
animal and plant species on campus to assess the balance of the campus ecosystem
m) Supporting sustainability by reducing carbon emissions and ensuring energy savings in buildings, introducing and
promoting the use of electric vehicles to reduce emissions, encouraging the use of electric vehicles, reducing the use of
vehicles for short distances and encouraging university residents to walk for a healthy life, taking initiatives to expand
the use of bicycles, providing suggestions to save heat and electricity in buildings and infrastructure , and monitoring
the impact on sustainability
n) Acting together with the Zero Waste Commission regarding waste treatment, evaluating the applicability of
composting and waste -to-energy projects on campus, organizing seminars to raise awareness about solar energy and
other clean energies, and encouraging projects
o) Contributing to social responsibility projects with other institutions and organizations outside the university
m) Supporting local production in the field of responsible consumption and production, ensuring students'
participation in workshops and organizing seminars on sustainable agriculture
p) Reflecting the understanding of sustainability primarily to the Gebze region and informing high school and primary
school students to raise public awareness
q) Monitoring the activities of student societies and clubs, ensuring that the activities are presented in a more

SECTION THREE
Structure, Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities of the Coordination Office
Structure of the Coordination Office
Article 7- (1) The structure of the Coordination Office is as follows:
a) Sustainability Coordination Office is a division under the University Research and Development Commission. The
Coordination O ffice consists of the coordinator, academic, technical and administrative staff , and members of the
Commission. If needed, work groups may be formed under the Commission.
b) The Coordinator is assigned by the Rector for three years from among the university faculty members specialized in
the fields of sustainability. The Coordinator whose term of office expires may be reassigned in the same manner. The
Coordinator reports to the relevant ice-rector responsible for the Coordinat ion Office and the Rector for the regular
execution and development of the works of the Coordination Office.
c) The Coordination Office carries out its activities jointly with the Commission.
d) The Coordinator proposes at least one person from among the university faculty members to be assigned by the
Rector as an assistant coordinator for a period of three years to assist him/her in his/her work. The Coordinator is
deputized by his/her assistant when he/she is not on duty. In the event that the deputy duty lasts longer than six
months, a new Coordinator is assigned in the same manner. In the event that the Coordinator's term of office expires or
he/she leaves his/her position for any reason, the duty of the assistant coordinator also ends.
e) The academic, technical, and administrative staff needs of the Coordinat ion Office are met by the personnel to be
assigned by the Rector. Part-time or volunteer students may also take part in the projects, activities , or research of the
Coordination Office.
Duties, Authorities, and Responsibilities of the Coordinator
Article 8-(1) The duties, authorities, and responsibilities of the Coordinator are as follows:
a) To represent the Coordination Office
b) To set the agenda of the Commission and implement the decisions taken
c) To carry out the necessary studies to realize the objectives of the Coordinat ion Office and to dev elop projects on
related issues
d) To submit the annual activity report of the Coordination Office to the Rectorate
e) To prepare the next year's work program in line with the opinion of the Commission regarding the work of the
Coordination Office
f) To carry out the necessary informative , consciousness-raising and awareness-raising activities so that internal and
external stakeholders are aware of the university's sustainable green campus policies and practices based on them
g) To plan training activities related to its area of activity and submit them to the Rectorate for approval, to organize
the approved training and seminar activities
h) To work in cooperation with the relevant centers, commissions, and divisions to take and implement measures to
reduce waste generation and water and energy consumption
i) To follow the changes in laws and regulations related to the field of duty and to carry out studies related to them
Sustainable Campus Commission
Article 9-(1) The structure of the Sustainable Campus Commission is as follows:
a) The Sustainable Campus Commission consists of the Supreme Commission and other commission members. The
Supreme Commission consists of the Vice-Rector, Secretary -General, Coordinator, a minimum of one assistant
coordinator, a minimum of three and a maximum of nine commission members, and a student representative to be
designated by the Sustainable Development Club advisor. The members of the Sustainability Commission consist of
faculty members who have studies related to the area of activity of the Coordination Office or who wish to contribute
voluntarily, and a student representative.
b) The term of assignment is 3 years and the member whose term expires may be rea ssigned. A new member is
assigned to complete the remaining term in place of the member who leaves before the end of the term.

c) The Commission convenes every three months in an ordinary manner and extraordinarily upon the invitation of the
Coordinator or upon the request of 2/3 of the members under the chairpersonship of the Coordination Office . The
quorum for the meeting is more than half of the number of members present. Decisions are taken by the majority of
those attending the meeting. Abstentions cannot be used in voting at meetings. In case of equality, the chairman's vote
counts as two votes. At the end of the meeting, the decisions taken regarding the issues discussed are finalized in a
minute signed by all members. The Commission may hold its meetings with the participation of internal and external
stakeholders if needed.
Duties of the Supreme Commission
Article 10-(1) The duties of the Supreme Commission are as follows:
a) To take decisions regarding the work of the Coordination Office
b) To discuss and decide on the suggestions of the Commission members
c) To establish work groups and taking decisions on determining the working principles of these work groups
d) To determine the principles of cooperation for joint studies to be carried out with national and international
institutions and organizations, to examine the protocols prepared, and to present opinions
e) To make internal arrangements and determine principles when deemed necessary regarding t he work of the
Coordination Office
Work Groups
Article 11-(1) Work groups are as follows:
a) Work groups may be decided to be formed by the Sustainability Coordination Office upon the proposal of the
Supreme Commission. The work groups consist of academic staff specialized in the relevant fiel ds selected from
among the Commission members and administrative staff who can work on the subject.
b) Work groups shall carry out their activities according to the procedures and principles determined.
c) The term of office of the a ssigned members is 3 years. The member whose term expires may be reassigned. A new
member is assigned to complete the remaining term in place of the member who leaves before the end of the term.
SECTION FOUR
Final Provisions
Cases Without Provision
Article 12-(1) In cases where there is no provision in this Directive, the provisions of the relevant legislation shall
apply with the decision of the Senate.
Enforcement
Article 13-(1) This Directive enters into force as of the date of adoption by the University Senate.
Execution
Article 14-(1) The provisions of this Directive shall be executed by the Rector of GTU.
Senate Adoption of the Directive
